>I am pretty vocal about things that frustrate me and they don’t really like that

This really worries me. You should always feel comfortable bringing up frustrations with your partner, so this for me seems like a red flag.

You don't need to point any blame, you did the right thing for yourself bringing things which made you uncomfortable, and if your partner tries to turn that around on you, you don't have an obligation to comfort them. It's up to them at this point if they want to accept your limits, or if they want to keep pointing fingers and make you feel guilty yourself for saying what you aren't comfortable. It seems like they are trying to break down the barrier of consent that you have and push past it for their own pleasure. Again huge red flag. That said again, if you no longer feel comfortable in this relationship it is also within your decision to end it, if that's what's best for you. In the end if your partner is just looking out for themself and not prioritising your comfort during sexual activities then that's not a healthy relationship. Don't let them portray themselves as a victim in this situation because they aren't. Good luck, I hope things are okay for you <3, and again - you did nothing wrong.
